statement: Half of the children on a bus are boys. Half of the boys wear caps. 3 boys wear caps. How many children are on the bus?

choices.misconception: I answered with the 3 boys who wear caps instead of all the children on the bus.
I doubled once to find the boys and then stopped.
I added the 3 boys with caps to the 6 boys.
I doubled three times instead of two times.

hints: Start from the 3 boys with caps and work backwards.
Work backwards one step at a time. The boys with caps are half of the boys, so find the boys first. Then the boys are half of the children, so find all the children.
If 3 is half of the boys, there are 6 boys. Now 6 is half of the children on the bus.

solutions.reliable: The 3 boys with caps are half of the boys, so there are 3 + 3 = 6 boys. The 6 boys are half of the children, so there are 6 + 6 = 12 children on the bus. The idea to keep: when a half is given, double to get back to the whole, one step at a time.
solutions.elegant: The boys with caps are half of a half, which is a quarter of the children. If a quarter is 3, the whole bus has 4 x 3 = 12 children.

whyOnTest: Undoing two halves in a row checks that a child can work backwards from a part to the whole without stopping early.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
